title: A Tide for the Summer
premise: Sable Thackeray built a career staging other people's perfect days while keeping his own heart archived — until a water-stained letter, mailed eleven years ago and never delivered, surfaces in the attic of the coastal inn where he's planning the summer festival's flagship wedding. The letter is from Jonah Reyes, the man who vanished from Sable's life a decade ago, confessing a truth that would have changed everything. As festival week unfolds, Sable must decide whether to expose the corruption that destroyed them both — risking the business empire he built on silence — or let the tide carry the past away again. He chooses truth: the wedding collapses, his partnership dissolves, but on the last night of the festival, on the empty beach, he and Jonah begin something honest at last.
about_author: Coral Delacroix spent seven years coordinating weddings along the Atlantic seaboard before trading clipboards for manuscripts. She writes love stories for people who swore off believing in them.

chapters.title: Watermarks
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. While inventorying the Saltglass Inn's attic for the Merrow Festival wedding, Sable finds a sealed letter postmarked eleven years ago, addressed to him in handwriting he'd know anywhere. He doesn't open it. Emotional beat: dread disguised as professionalism; the past knocking politely.

chapters.title: The Perfect Machine
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Flashbacks interleave with present-day chaos as Sable manages demanding clients and his controlling business partner Vivian Marsh, who saved him from ruin years ago and never lets him forget it. Emotional beat: we see the gilded cage — loyalty purchased with silence.

chapters.title: Jonah, Present Tense
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah returns to town as the festival's new harbormaster, having spent eleven years at sea outrunning what he did. Seeing Sable across the docks, he realizes the letter he mailed never arrived. Emotional beat: hope colliding with guilt.

chapters.title: Eleven Years of Weather
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Forced together by festival logistics, Sable and Jonah circle each other with old wounds showing as sharp banter. A storm strands them in the inn's boathouse, and Sable finally opens the letter. Emotional beat: the confession inside reframes everything — Jonah left to protect Sable from Vivian's fraud scheme.

chapters.title: What Vivian Knew
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah investigates whether Vivian's development company is quietly buying out the inn and the waterfront — the same scheme he discovered a decade ago, now nearly complete. He finds Sable's name on documents he never signed knowingly. Emotional beat: protective fury hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Rehearsal Dinner
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The festival wedding's rehearsal dinner becomes a minefield when Vivian arrives unannounced and performs warmth while privately reminding Sable who owns his career. Sable lies to Jonah about it afterward. Emotional beat: the cost of survival made visible; loyalty curdling.

chapters.title: Low Tide Confessions
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. At low tide, Jonah shows Sable the deeds and shell companies proving Vivian intends to raze the harbor district after the festival. Sable's denial cracks — he recognizes his own signature on papers he was told were routine. Emotional beat: betrayal of self, not just by others.

chapters.title: The Contract
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Vivian offers Sable full partnership and the festival contract renewed for five years — if he signs one more document and keeps quiet through the weekend. Alone with the pen in hand, Sable remembers who he was before she saved him. Emotional beat: the darkest hour; choosing between the life he built and the man he might be.

chapters.title: A Tide for the Summer
chapters.summary: Both POVs converge. During the wedding ceremony itself, Sable walks to the front — not to object, but to publicly resign and read the eleven-year-old letter aloud, exposing Vivian's scheme to the assembled town. Chaos erupts; Vivian threatens ruin; the couple, moved rather than ruined, stands with him. Emotional beat: climax — truth spoken at the worst possible moment, which turns out to be the only right one.

chapters.title: After the Festival
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Weeks later: the deal collapsed under scrutiny, Sable is rebuilding as an independent planner, and the harbor district is organizing to save itself. On the emptied beach after the season's last fireworks, Jonah asks nothing except a first date, eleven years late. Sable says yes. Emotional beat: resolution — love begun in truth, not rescue.
